blocks.content: The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial authority in the country. It acts as the guardian of the Constitution and protector of Fundamental Rights. The provisions related to the Supreme Court are given in Part V, Chapter IV of the Constitution (Articles 124–147).
1. Constitutional Articles Related to the Supreme Court

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Articles 124 to 147 in Part V of the Indian Constitution deal with the Supreme Court's organization, independence, jurisdiction, powers, and procedures.
Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President of India after consultation with members of the judiciary as per the Collegium system.

To be appointed as a Supreme Court judge, a person must be a citizen of India and have served as a High Court judge for 5 years, or an advocate in a High Court for 10 years, or be a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President.
A Supreme Court judge can be removed from office only by an order of the President after an address by Parliament supported by a special majority on grounds of proven misbehaviour or incapacity.
The Supreme Court possesses Original Jurisdiction (Article 131), Appellate Jurisdiction (Articles 132–136), Advisory Jurisdiction (Article 143), and Writ Jurisdiction (Article 32).

cells: Supreme Court as a Court of Record
Law declared by Supreme Court binding on all courts

blocks.content: 2. Composition of the Supreme Court
• The Supreme Court consists of the Chief Justice of India and other judges.
• Originally the Constitution provided for 1 Chief Justice and 7 judges.
• At present the sanctioned strength is 34 judges including the Chief Justice.
3. Appointment of Judges
• The judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President of India.
• The Chief Justice is appointed by the President.
• The collegium system plays an important role in the appointment process.
4. Qualifications of Supreme Court Judges
• Must be a citizen of India.
• Must have been a judge of a High Court for at least 5 years.
The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial court and the final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
• OR must have been an advocate of a High Court for at least 10 years.
• OR must be a distinguished jurist.
5. Tenure of Judges
• Supreme Court judges hold office until the age of 65 years.
• They can resign by writing to the President.
• They can be removed through impeachment.
6. Removal of Judges
• Judges can be removed only by impeachment.

rows: Exclusive power to settle federal disputes between the Centre and States or between States.
Power to issue writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Certiorari, etc.) for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
Hears appeals against High Court judgments in constitutional, civil, criminal cases, and Special Leave Petitions.
President can refer matters of law or fact of public importance to the court for its opinion.

blocks.content: • Impeachment requires a special majority in both Houses of Parliament.
• The grounds for removal are proved misbehavior or incapacity.
7. Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
Original Jurisdiction (Article 131)
Disputes between the Union and States or between States.
Appellate Jurisdiction
Appeals from High Courts in constitutional, civil and criminal matters.
Advisory Jurisdiction (Article 143)
The President can seek the opinion of the Supreme Court.
8. Writ Jurisdiction

items: Article 32 grants citizens the right to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
Article 143 allows the President to seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion, but the opinion provided is advisory and not binding on the President.
A motion for the removal of a Supreme Court judge must be signed by at least 100 members in the Lok Sabha or 50 members in the Rajya Sabha.

blocks.content: The Supreme Court can issue writs under Article 32 for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

blocks.content: EXAM Important Facts
• Supreme Court established in 1950.
• Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary.
• Judges retire at age 65.
• Article 32 is called the heart and soul of the Constitution.
